objective: `scripts/make_sample_data.py` builds the whole sample data set in one long `build` function and writes the stock file by hand, line by line, because `stockroom/csvio.py` has a reader for the stock file but no writer. Add `write_stock(levels)` to `stockroom/csvio.py`, the counterpart of `read_stock`, and split the script's `build` into one function per file that uses it. This is a pure refactor: for the same seed and order count the script writes byte-identical files, and the existing tests keep passing without being edited.
acceptance: `csvio.write_stock(levels)` takes an iterable of `(sku, on_hand, reserved)` rows and returns the stock file text: the header line `sku,on_hand,reserved` and one line per row, every line ending in a newline; `read_stock(write_stock(levels))` returns the rows, and an empty iterable gives the header line only

The script defines `make_items(rng)`, `make_stock(rng, items)`, `make_orders(rng, items, count)` and still `build(seed, orders)`; `make_items` returns the list of `Item` records, `make_stock` the list of `(sku, on_hand, reserved)` rows and `make_orders` the list of `Order` records

Calling `make_items`, `make_stock` and `make_orders` in this order on one `random.Random(seed)` produces exactly the records that `build(seed, count)` writes, and the builders draw only from the generator they are given (they never touch the global `random` state)

The generator is used in the same order as before, so the files written for the same seed and order count are byte for byte the same: `build` returns the same three texts for seeds and counts such as (7, 20), (3, 9) and (11, 0), and `python scripts/make_sample_data.py --out DIR --seed 3 --orders 9` prints the same line and writes the same files
`build` writes the stock text with `write_stock`; the script no longer contains string literals that spell out the stock file's columns
